source.title: Preemptive LLM Unlearning against Forbidden Capability Acquisition via Gradient Sealing
source.authors: Ke-Mou Li; Qi-Zhou Wang; Yue Wang; Feng-Peng Li; Zhuan Shi; Negar Rostamzadeh; Golnoosh Farnadi; Masashi Sugiyama; Jian-Tao Zhou

record.tranche_reason: The study uses downstream fine-tuning as an acquisition attack to evaluate its preemptive-unlearning defense. It measures forbidden-capability acquisition, not harmful-request refusals or the token-position KL and compliant-opening effects in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses safety loss after fine-tuning in related work and cites prior studies, but those cited results are not this study's results. Its own results concern acquisition or restoration of forbidden-domain capabilities, plus local gate measurements. These are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure the safety/refusal behaviors named by V1–V7.
record.test_reason: The study measures forbidden-knowledge acquisition: TOFU extraction strength and WMDP accuracy after fine-tuning on forbidden-domain data. It does not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance, per-token KL, prefilling or decoding bypasses, or where safety is localized. Qi et al. (2024) is cited only as motivation and related work. Its fine-tuning attacks serve to evaluate its own unlearning defense (GSU) against unlearning baselines. No version names a forbidden-knowledge capability, so the study does not use the claim's finding as a tool either. This makes it cites_only/T6 rather than uses_without_test/T4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that pre-release defenses must seal the gradient pathways that later fine-tuning would use, not only suppress current outputs. They report that GSU limits forbidden acquisition while keeping benign fine-tunability, and treat the mechanism evidence as local, not proof of irreversible resistance.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops preemptive unlearning using proxy look-ahead, selected-gate sealing, response suppression, and retain supervision. It does not reproduce the cited safety fine-tuning or response-token KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different outcomes across prevention settings, models, domains, and attack checkpoints. Its supplementary analyses use single runs and fixed configurations; the authors note that results are not independent replications and that acquisition gaps can narrow over the attack budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Retrospective unlearning (NPO, RMU) leaves knowledge reacquirable by fine-tuning. On Qwen3.5-2B, NPO extraction strength rose from 0.112 to 0.326 and RMU from 0.032 to 0.257 after the same acquisition attack.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level unlearning is shallow: suppressed knowledge is reacquired by brief fine-tuning, an analogue of V1 for knowledge rather than refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: GSU reduces forbidden-capability acquisition under fine-tuning attacks in several settings. Proxy-identified channels predict where acquisition flows (pooled ρ = 0.617).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Acquisition-sensitive pathways can be localized and attenuated to resist forbidden-capability fine-tuning.

record.problems: The paper states that all reported runs use seed 0 and that supplementary observations have no multi-seed error bars or significance tests. TOFU splits are record-disjoint but share authors and domain structure; the authors say this does not establish unseen-author or semantically disjoint-fact generalization. Gate probes are local measurements, not whole-network gradients, and the study says they do not prove causal isolation or irreversible resistance. The full fine-tuning protocols and utility thresholds limit what can be inferred about unrestricted retraining.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within a focused set of adjacent-construct results, omitted most model-by-setting entries from Table 1, the remaining Table 2 metrics, the full attack trajectories and component-ablation values in §§5.3 and F.1–F.7, and additional gate statistics in Figures 9–11 and Tables 5–9. These results concern forbidden-capability acquisition, utility, or local mechanism measures and do not test V1–V7's specified safety/refusal outcomes.

untested.parts: Harmful-request compliance after harmful fine-tuning of safety-trained models.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Localization of safety or refusal behaviour in weights.
Deep safety alignment and its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: Relation and tranche are changed from uses_without_test/T4 to cites_only/T6. The only links to the claim are citations of Qi et al. 2024 and Lermen et al. in the introduction and related work (§B.2), which the paper says concern broad safety alignment or refusal. All experiments are knowledge-unlearning benchmarks (TOFU, WMDP), and no refusal or safety metric is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-request refusal or compliance by safety-trained models after fine-tuning on harmful examples.
Whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful-request compliance; the benign task measures adaptation and subsequent forbidden-capability acquisition, not refusal rates.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models over response positions.
Compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety/refusal behavior. Selected-gate probes concern acquisition pathways, not safety behavior.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety behavior to be shallow.
Whether safety training spread beyond initial response tokens deepens safety or holds up under bypasses.

relation.reason: The introduction and §B.2 cite safety erosion under fine-tuning as background; the study neither tests that behavior nor uses shallow safety alignment as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: The results measure forbidden-knowledge acquisition and selected-gate mechanisms, not the harmful compliance, refusal, token-position concentration, or safety localization named by V1–V7.

source_check.notes: The authors’ conclusion paraphrase is accurate; method-performance and local gate diagnostics provide no verdict on V1–V7. The r8–r9 verdict-fix descriptions should say acquisition, not reacquisition: the retain-only Reference had no training exposure to the target splits (§3.2; §E.1).
